item.title: Together AI releases Hallmark anti‑AI‑slop design skill for Claude, Cursor, Codex
item.description:
Together AI releases Hallmark anti‑AI‑slop design skill for Claude, Cursor, Codex

Together AI has launched Hallmark, an anti‑AI‑slop design skill that works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode and refuses to look AI‑generated.

🧩 How it works

  • Hallmark starts with a hard floor that never ships (e.g., contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, broken phone layout). It then steps aside.
  • Gates are organised in tiers:
    • Reflex gates are the defaults a model falls into; a reasoned build can over‑rule them.
    • Finish checks are craft‑detail validations that never block a ship.
  • A page is built from the job itself (booking page books, shop sells, newsletter subscribes). The action appears where the category dictates and the page ends on that action.
  • Hallmark selects three themes from a catalog of forty‑eight materials (paper, type, colour, surfaces, etc.). Each theme is a material file (≤ 8 KB) with a picture; the build reads exactly one.
  • The system lints the result in a real browser, looking for typical AI‑generated tells such as:
    • eyebrow above every heading
    • tracked‑capital labels
    • a single coloured word in a headline
    • pages of empty frames or only photographs
    • hero images that miss the screen
    • email sign‑up at the end of every page
    • forms that say “thanks” without actually sending anything.
  • A fresh‑context reviewer gets the final word before shipping.

⚙️ Key details

  • 48 themes – each a material with its own picture of a finished page.
  • Real photographs – 755 openly‑licensed photos are selected per subject and credited on the page.
  • Custom mode – say custom and Hallmark drops the themes, using only the floor, gates and a short direction file to generate a unique page.
  • Real product integration – point Hallmark at a URL, dev server, or app and it captures screenshots itself.
  • Redesign & audit commands:
    • /hallmark redesign <path> rebuilds a page while preserving content and wiring.
    • /hallmark audit <path> reports issues without changing the page.
  • Pre‑flight reads the project (fonts, palette, framework, locked design.md) and asks once for the material (photos, screenshots, real numbers). Nothing is invented.
  • Scripts – scripts/theme.mjs deal offers three fitting themes and clears the log; draw constructs the page anatomy from its job.

Gate summary

Gate Description
Floor Hard floor that never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, broken phone layout).
Reflex Default gates a model falls into; a build with reason may over‑rule one on the record.
Finish Craft‑detail checks that never block a ship.

🔧 Usage

  • Invoke Hallmark with a prompt; it designs a page using the same rules and checks applied to the themed builds.
  • For custom pages, provide only a direction file; Hallmark generates a page without pre‑defined components or palette recipes.
  • Use the CLI commands (/hallmark redesign, /hallmark audit) to iterate or inspect existing pages.

📚 Resources

  • Explore all 48 themes at usehallmark.com.
  • Theme files live in skills/hallmark/references/themes/ with accompanying images.
  • Direction guidelines are in skills/hallmark/references/direction.md.

#AIdesign #TogetherAI #HallmarkSkill

Source: Nutlope/hallmark

item.title: Canva launches Canva Craft AI image generation model
item.description:
Canva launches Canva Craft AI image generation model

Canva announced the launch of Canva Craft, an AI image‑generation model that directly competes with offerings from OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google.

🔍 Overview

  • Canva Craft uses a two‑stage architecture that plans a design before generating an image, providing greater precision, consistency and control.
  • The model is positioned as Canva’s first AI image model that plans designs before generation.

🧩 How it works

  • The two‑stage system first creates a layout plan, then renders the final image, which helps it generate complex images that require legible text and precise object placement.
  • Canva trained Craft on “millions of human‑made templates” from its library, including social media posts, presentations, infographics, and menus.

⚙️ Key details

  • Generates images up to 2K resolution.
  • Supports more than 30 aspect ratios.
  • Capable of creating social media posts, marketing content, realistic scenes, digital art, environmental imagery, and more.
  • Includes layers for AI‑generated images, allowing edits to parts of an image while leaving the rest untouched.
  • Built on prompt‑based editing capabilities launched in April, which let users describe changes to a design.
  • Ranked fourth on Design Arena’s leaderboard for the best AI image generation models, behind OpenAI’s GPT‑Image‑2.5 Sunburst, GPT‑Image‑2.5 Flare, and GPT‑Image‑2.
  • Provides robust input and output moderation, privacy and safety controls, and reporting tools.
  • Future roadmap includes AI agents plugging into Canva Craft via the open Model Context Protocol and the rollout of faster variants (Craft‑fast and Craft‑ultrafast).
Rank Model
1 OpenAI GPT‑Image‑2.5 Sunburst
2 OpenAI GPT‑Image‑2.5 Flare
3 OpenAI GPT‑Image‑2
4 Canva Craft

🚀 Availability

  • Canva Craft is available now to all users globally.
  • To try it, open Canva, click the three‑dot option on the left‑hand menu, and select Dream Lab.

💡 Why it matters

  • By planning designs before rendering, Canva Craft aims to give designers more control over AI‑generated visuals, addressing common challenges such as text legibility and object placement.
  • The model expands Canva’s AI portfolio, complementing earlier features like prompt‑based editing and layered image manipulation.
  • Ranking fourth on a crowdsourced benchmark shows Canva’s growing competitiveness in the AI image‑generation space.

#Canva #AIImageGeneration #DesignAI

Source: Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them

item.title: OpenDesign Launches Local-First Open-Source Alternative to Claude Design
item.description:
OpenDesign Launches Local-First Open-Source Alternative to Claude Design

OpenDesign has launched as an open-source, local-first desktop application for macOS and Windows that serves as an alternative to Claude Design.

🔍 Overview

OpenDesign is a native desktop app used to create and refine various digital assets within a project’s Studio. Users can start with a brief, utilize reusable skills in Plugins, and convert brand references into a design system via brand-grade DESIGN.md files.

🧩 How it works

OpenDesign operates as a local-first app that supports a wide range of runtimes and endpoints:

  • Native Runtimes: Supports DeepSeek Harness (dsh), Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Qwen, Copilot, Amp, Hermes, Kimi, Antigravity, and 26 distinct local CLI executables.
  • BYOK: Supports any OpenAI-compatible endpoint via Bring Your Own Key (BYOK).
  • DeepSeek Integration: The official dsh agent harness connects as a native runtime providing model discovery, tool calls, structured thinking, session resume, and cancellation.

⚙️ Key details

Users can utilize a single recharge to access both agent and image models within the application:

Model Type Supported Models
Agents GPT, Claude, DeepSeek
Images GPT Image 2.0, Seedream 5.0 Pro, Nano Banana 2.0

Capabilities and Exports:

  • Generates: Web, desktop, and mobile prototypes; live dashboards/artifacts; decks; images; video; and HyperFrames motion graphics.
  • Artifacts: Delivers single-page artifacts using real CSS, real fonts, and real components.
  • Preview & Export: Features a sandboxed iframe preview with exports available in HTML, PDF, PPTX, and MP4 formats.
  • Workflow: Generated files remain in the OpenDesign workflow for delivery and live preview.

🚀 Availability

DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro are now available. OpenDesign members can use both of these models without limits for two weeks directly inside the app.

#OpenDesign #DeepSeek #OpenSource #AIagents #UIUX

Source: nexu-io/open-design
